quality.location: app/src/main.ts reset() and session onState; app/src/flight-trace.ts record()
quality.description: Restarting while flying can leave the new flight with a poisoned or empty review trace. reset() calls flightTrace.clear() and session.pause()/session.reset() synchronously. Worker state messages already queued from the old flight are delivered after reset() returns. Because reviewing is false, they are recorded into the cleared trace. FlightTrace.record() then rejects every new-flight state whose step or t_s is at or below that stale tail. It never recovers until the next clear(). Review could then show the previous flight's states, or record nothing for the new flight. Expected: the trace drops stale-generation states, or clears when the first post-reset state arrives. Reproduction: hold a flight key while flying, press R or Restart, Start, fly, then open Review and check that the bounds start near t_s=0 of the new flight. Whether session.ts already filters stale messages cannot be checked, because session.ts is not in this packet.
quality.evidence: main.ts reset(): `flightTrace.clear(); ... session.pause(); ... session.reset()`; onState: `if (!reviewing) flightTrace.record(...)`; flight-trace.ts: `if (snapshot.step <= latest.step || snapshot.t_s <= latest.t_s) return false;`. The smoke test only checks review clearing after a reset from the paused state.

quality.location: app/src/aircraft-visual.ts header comment; app/src/scene.ts Model.fromGltfAsync and modelHpr
quality.description: The aircraft visual is authored with +x forward and +z right in glTF axes. Cesium's Model loader assumes a glTF forward axis of +Z by default and converts it to Cesium +X. No forwardAxis is passed. The chase-view aircraft may therefore render yawed by 90° relative to the camera and the JSBSim heading. The heading mapping `heading_rad - π/2` assumes model +X is forward. Expected: pass `forwardAxis: Axis.X` (or author the model with +Z forward), and add a recorded orientation check such as a chase screenshot or a model-matrix assertion.

quality.description: Missing JSBSim properties are not detected. Only systems/automatic-mixture-enabled is checked with HasNode. GetPropertyValue on a missing node typically returns 0, and the bridge converts that into plausible readings: oil and EGT become 0 °F = 255.37 K, which engineFields accepts because it only requires > 0 K. Oil pressure, fuel flow and tank contents become 0, which passes the >= 0 checks. A misnamed property would therefore show a fabricated indication instead of 'unavailable'. Examples are fuel-flow-rate-gph, tank[n]/contents-volume-gal, oil-pressure-psi and egt-degF. The browser test cannot catch this. It only asserts finite and >= 0. Its fuel display assertions compare the display against the same telemetry value, so they test the unit conversion, not the source. The mixture-cutoff check (fuel_flow_m3ps === 0) can pass vacuously because fuel flow is never shown to be > 0 before cutoff. Expected: HasNode checks returning NaN for missing properties, which engineFields then rejects. The test should assert positive fuel flow and a plausible oil temperature/EGT while running rich, before checking cutoff.
quality.evidence: bridge.cpp gf_engine_state values[4..9]; engine.js engineFields bounds (values[5] <= 0 || values[6] <= 0); engine-smoke.mjs initial telemetry loop (>= 0 only) and the cutoff wait.

quality.description: The native study tests are not shown to run in any recorded gate. This covers altimeter.test.mjs, cockpit.test.mjs, engine.test.mjs and prepare-aircraft.test.py. The hyphenated name prepare-aircraft.test.py would not be found by default unittest discovery (pattern test*.py). The DONE counts of '39/65/70 native tests' and 'five adapter tests' are therefore only author claims. quality.description: The integrator reset may do nothing. It writes '.../initial-integrator-value' only if HasNode finds it. That is a PID configuration element, not a known runtime reset property; JSBSim PIDs normally reset through a trigger property. If the node is absent, wind-up can carry over between wings-level and heading modes, and nothing reports the failed reset. Expected: reset through the PID's actual trigger/reset property, or fail or log when no reset node exists. A test should check that ap_aileron_norm starts near zero after a mode change.

quality.location: studies/e1-browser/sim/cockpit.js cockpitFields; bridge.cpp gf_set_autopilot/gf_init heading wrap

quality.description: Per-wheel and structure-contact identities come from hard-coded gear-unit indices. Units 0–2 are assumed to be nose/left/right and units 3–5 tail/left wingtip/right wingtip. The only guard is GetNumGearUnits() == 6, so a reordered or edited c172x gear file would silently mislabel wheel loads and STRUCTURE CONTACT text in the UI. Expected: bind each index to the model's contact names (for example FGLGear::GetName()) or assert the order in a test. Reproduction: swap two <contact> entries in the c172x ground_reactions block. The count stays 6 and the labels swap with no error.
quality.evidence: bridge.cpp gf_ground_state: `GetGearUnit(i + 3)->GetWOW()` → mask bits 1/2/4 and `GetGearUnit(i)` → nose/left/right. landing-feedback.ts maps bits to TAIL/LEFT WINGTIP/RIGHT WINGTIP. No c172x gear XML or name assertion is in the packet. landing-physics.mjs indirectly checks only that right wheel (index 2) contacts first under right bank.

quality.description: The landing fixture does not exercise several behaviors it is cited for. (1) structure_mask_seen is accumulated but never asserted, so structure-contact indication has no runtime test. (2) The 120/240 Hz convergence differences are computed but have no tolerance assertion, so step-size consistency is reported, not tested (R-SIM-5 requires tolerances chosen before execution). (3) The steering check compares heading change at rudder ±0.35 but does not verify nosewheel contact or isolate steering from aerodynamic rudder yaw. It cannot show that the steer-cmd-norm coupling contributes or has the right sign. (4) The script imports the built JSBSim dist and is not part of the shared or hosted gate.

quality.description: The dialog notes can say 'Flight continues while this panel is open.' while the flight is paused. Both components use the single `running` flag for two purposes: enabling controls and choosing the note text. The packet's own tests require the radio and NAV controls to stay enabled while paused, so `running` must be true when paused. That leaves the 'Flight is paused.' branch reachable only when the engine is not ready. Reproduction: start the app (initially paused) or pause in flight, use a viewport of 900 px or less, and open Radio/NAV or NAV instruments. The note claims flight continues. Expected: the note reflects the actual paused or flying state, which needs a separate paused/flying input distinct from 'controls allowed'.

'Flight continues while this panel is open.' : 'Flight is paused.'`. navigation-gauges.ts: `canAdjust = !!config && running && !reviewing` with the same note ternary. avionics-smoke.mjs asserts `${id} is available while paused` for nav-obs/nav-demo before Start and after #pause. navigation-input.browser.mjs asserts gauge OBS buttons are enabled while paused.

quality.description: Retry stops working if resume() never settles. unlock() keeps the single in-flight promise in `unlocking` and returns it to every later call until it settles. The project's own research note says resume() 'may remain pending when activation is unavailable'. If the first resume() stays pending (no real activation, activation already consumed, or some browser policies), `unlocking` never clears. The status stays 'locked'. Every later speaker-button or volume retry returns the same stale promise and never calls context.resume() again. That breaks the R-AUDIO-1 'accurate audio status and retry path'. Expected: each trusted retry calls resume() on the existing context, or a pending attempt is bounded by a timeout or statechange. Reproduction: stub AudioContext.prototype.resume to return a never-settling promise, click Start, then click #audio-toggle. Only one resume call happens and the status never leaves 'locked'.
quality.evidence: engine-audio.ts: `if (unlocking) return unlocking;` and `unlocking = attempt().finally(() => { unlocking = null; });` with `await context.resume();` inside attempt. docs/research/2026-11-02-engine-audio.md Web Audio lifecycle paragraph. engine-audio.browser.mjs tests only `resume = () => Promise.reject(...)`, never a pending resume.

quality.description: The worker throws away the availability result of the contact check. stateMessage() always spreads `...collision`, which starts as EMPTY_COLLISION (mask 0). That happens even when ground_collision is false or when groundCollisionContact() returns {available:false}, for example when structure_contact_mask is missing or outside 0..7. Live UI, session and the recorded trace then see collision_mask:0, which reads as a definitive 'clear', not 'unavailable'. Separately, if a contact is detected but collisionRecord() returns null (non-finite or missing pre-step ground motion), the contact is dropped silently and integration continues. Expected: unavailable contact telemetry is published or recorded as unavailable, for example by omitting the collision group or adding an availability flag. A detected contact with no valid pre-step motion should still halt, or should report an explicit unavailable/failed state. Reproduction from source: init with ground_collision:true on a native build whose structure_contact_mask is absent or >7 while ground_agl_m is present. Every state carries collision_mask:0. main.ts shows its unavailable notice only when collision_mask or ground_agl_m is undefined.
quality.evidence: worker.js stateMessage(): `...readEngineSwitchFields(), ...collision`; stepOnce(): `const record = contact.mask ? collisionRecord(...) : null; if (record) {...}` with no else branch; `contact.available` is never read. collision.js returns {available:false, mask:0} for invalid structure masks. main.ts onState notice condition: `state.collision_mask === undefined || state.ground_agl_m === undefined`.

quality.description: The proxy thresholds come only from the illustrative visual geometry. Nothing in the unit gate ties them to the native c172x CG-AGL at rest or under nose-strut compression. The packet's own formula gives propeller support of about 1.05 m when level and about 1.36 m at -0.1 rad pitch (0.0998*3.17 + 1.05*cos 0.1). The visual nose-wheel bottom is about 1.32 m below the origin. If the native rest AGL is close to that, a modest nose-down attitude during ordinary braking or a firm nose-wheel touchdown could latch a 'Propeller visual sample' collision. That would stop flight during ordinary wheel contact. The unit tests use hand-picked AGLs of 1.2/1.4 m. Only the unrecorded actual-browser run (a 600-step normal preset) addresses this. Expected: a gated check against native rest and compressed-strut AGL/pitch, or documented margins.
quality.evidence: collision.js prop support `dx * prop.x + prop.radius * hypot(dy, dz)`; aircraft-visual.ts nose wheel at y=-1.15, radius 0.17; collision.test.mjs uses `groundCollisionContact(1.2, 0, .07, 0)`; ground-collision.browser.mjs 'normal' baseline is not in the recorded gate.

quality.description: R-DATA-1 requires revision metadata for every shipped visual asset. The new airport photograph has no source revision, layer edition or retrieval date: `sourceImageDate` is null and no retrieval timestamp is recorded. It is an extract from a live WMS (`requestUrl` against `ogc-free-images.ows`, layer `he_dop_rgb`) whose content can change. Repeating the same request later can return different bytes, and the metadata cannot tell which edition was bundled. The terrain manifest records an edition (`2025H2`), so the two assets are inconsistent. Expected: record the retrieval date and any layer edition or capabilities timestamp the service exposes, or explicitly state that the revision is unknown and why.

quality.description: The renderer fetches and verifies its own copy of the terrain package with `loadTerrainPackage()`. The worker loads the package independently. `update()` never checks that the worker's active terrain id or sha256 matches `terrainGrid.id`/`sha256`. If the manifest is redeployed or cached differently between the two fetches, the rendered and native surfaces could differ silently, against R-WORLD-2's 'same SW–NE triangle surface'. Only the browser test compares the worker's `build.terrain.sha256` with a literal. Expected: fail closed when the worker's ready/build terrain hash differs from the renderer's grid.
quality.evidence: scene.ts: `const terrainGrid = await loadTerrainPackage()`. No comparison against state or worker terrain identity. public-terrain.browser.mjs checks `worldReady...build.terrain.sha256` against a constant only.

quality.description: The Cesium terrain provider uses a GeographicTilingScheme limited to the package rectangle with 1×1 level-zero tiles. Cesium derives globe level-zero tiles from the terrain provider's tiling scheme, so with public terrain active, no globe surface is expected outside 8.45–8.90E, 49.85–50.35N. Two consequences follow. Parts of the bundled overview photograph (8.40–8.45E, 49.80–49.85N) are no longer drawn. Near the package edges, for example looking north or west from the Taunus ridge, the horizon is likely to show background color instead of ground. This is unverified in the packet. Expected: confirm in an actual browser and either declare the visual edge or add a global fallback surface outside the package.
quality.evidence: terrain-provider.ts: `new GeographicTilingScheme({ rectangle, ... numberOfLevelZeroTilesX: 1, numberOfLevelZeroTilesY: 1 })`. scene.ts: `OVERVIEW = Rectangle.fromDegrees(8.4, 49.8, 8.9, 50.1)`. No browser observation of edge views is recorded.

quality.location: app/src/autopilot-panel.ts change()/click() selector branch; studies/e1-browser/sim/kap140.js show()/step() page expiry
quality.description: The shared selector field is interpreted by whatever `kap_display_page` the latest snapshot reports at commit time, not by the page that was shown when the user started editing. BARO (page 2) and VS (page 1) pages expire after 3 simulated seconds (`pageUntil = t + 3`, cleared in `step()` while running). render() keeps a focused field's text but changes its unit/label and readOnly state underneath it. Reproduction while running: press BARO, focus the selector, type `1013`, then blur more than 3 s later. Page is now 0, so change() sends `{action:'select-altitude', value: 1013*0.3048}`. If AP is engaged, `select-altitude` also sets `altArm=1`, so the aircraft can arm and capture an unintended ~1013 ft target. The reverse case, an altitude entry made while engagement or ALT→VS shows page 1, is rejected as readOnly. The +/− buttons have the same race. Expected: bind the entry to the page and units active at focus or pointer-down, or reject the commit when the page changed. A pressure value must never become an altitude command.
quality.evidence: autopilot-panel.ts change(): `latest!.kap_display_page === 2 ? baro-setting : select-altitude`; render() only rewrites value when not focused; kap140.js `show=(which,t)=>{page=which;pageUntil=t+3}`, `if (page && s.t_s>=pageUntil) page=0`, `case 'select-altitude': selected=c.value; if (engaged) altArm=1`. The browser tests exercise BARO entry only while paused, when page never expires.

quality.description: Arming NAV/APR/REV from HDG keeps HDG active (`latArm=mode; if (lat !== 1) lat=0`). Pressing the same key again to cancel the arm runs `lat=0; latArm=0`, which silently drops the active HDG mode to ROL. This is inconsistent with the arming path, and no source or test establishes it. Reproduction: AP engaged → HDG → NAV with |CDI|>0.5 (NAV ARM, HDG active) → NAV again. The aircraft reverts to wings-level ROL instead of remaining in HDG.
quality.evidence: kap140.js setNav: `if (lat === mode || latArm === mode) {lat=0; latArm=0; gsArm=0; return;}`; kap140.test.mjs has no cancel-arm case.

quality.location: studies/e1-browser/sim/kap140.js disconnect()/'ap' engage/GS recapture; app/src/autopilot-panel.ts render()
quality.description: Source-loss annunciations are never cleared by disconnect or re-engagement. disconnect() resets modes but not `latAlert`, `vertAlert` or `hdgPromptUntil`. The panel renders `ap-lateral-alert`/`ap-vertical-alert` regardless of `kap_engaged`. A flashing NAV or GS alert can therefore persist with AP OFF and carry into a new engagement. A GS alert also remains after automatic GS recapture. The only GS acknowledgment is a double ALT press within 1 s, which itself toggles the vertical mode twice. Expected: alerts scoped to the engagement and the active source condition, with tests for clearing.
quality.evidence: kap140.js `const disconnect = () => {engaged=0; lat=0; latArm=0; vert=0; altArm=0; gsArm=0; gesture=0; gsInhibited=false;}`; `'alt': if (s.t_s-lastAltPress <= 1 && vertAlert===2) vertAlert=0`; the GS recapture path does not reset vertAlert; the unit test re-captures GS without checking kap_vertical_alert.

quality.description: `step()` returns silently when sensors fail validation. Source-loss fallback, NAV/GS capture and ALT preselect capture are then skipped without annunciation while the previous guidance stays applied. One realistic trigger is `elevator_norm` (native `ap/elevator_cmd`) exceeding |1|. In that case kapFields() also throws 'Invalid autopilot instrument state' from postState, and createKap140 throws at init. Whether the adapter clamps `ap/elevator_cmd` to ±1 is not in this packet. Expected: an invalid sensor should produce a visible fallback or disconnect, not a silent skip.
quality.evidence: kap140.js `function step(s) { if (!validSensors(s)) return; ...}`; validSensors requires `Math.abs(s.elevator_norm) <= 1`; worker kapSensors passes `M.HEAPF64[pointer + 2]` (ap/elevator_cmd).

quality.location: kap140.js 'vertical' in ALT; worker.js onKap140 envelope; bridge.cpp gf_set_autopilot_vertical; worker.js applyKapGuidance
quality.description: Bounds are inconsistent across layers. UP/DN taps in ALT clamp the hold to −2000..20000 m pressure altitude, while select-altitude is limited to −2000..11000 m pressure by the worker. The native ALT target is limited to −2500..20000 m physical, computed as `physical + hold − pressure`. A hold outside the native range causes applyKapGuidance to call fail() and stop the flight, instead of rejecting the command. This is practically unreachable in a C172, but the validation is not coherent.
quality.evidence: kap140.js `hold=clamp(hold+dir*20*FT,-2000,20000)`; worker `outsidePressureEnvelope = pressureTarget < -2000 || pressureTarget > 11000` only for select-altitude/baro-setting; bridge `mode == 2 && (target < -2500.0 || target > 20000.0)` → worker `fail('Autopilot controller target unavailable; flight stopped.')`.

quality.description: The sign conventions for `cdi_norm` and `gs_norm` are not declared, contrary to R-SIM-3. GS guidance adds `gs_norm*3` m/s, so positive gs_norm commands a climb, but no contract says whether positive means below or above the glidepath. No live GS source exists, so only synthetic unit values exercise it.
quality.evidence: kap140.d.ts nav fields untyped beyond number; kap140.js `clamp(gsBase+s.nav.gs_norm*3, VS_MIN, VS_MAX)`; navigation.js always returns gs_norm 0.

quality.description: `hdgPromptUntil = t+5` is set on every NAV/APR/REV press that reaches the body, including deselection and invalid-source presses. The 5 s HDG prompt therefore flashes when cancelling a mode or when the source is invalid, not only for DG course selection.
quality.evidence: kap140.js setNav: the prompt is set before the `lat === mode || latArm === mode` cancel branch and before the `!sourceOK` branch.

quality.description: The panel's keydown handler calls preventDefault on every repeated key, including inside the selector and heading number inputs. Held Backspace and held ArrowUp/ArrowDown value spinning therefore do not work in those fields. Shortcut isolation only needs stopPropagation for inputs.

quality.description: Every init sets `regional_navigation: true`, including Egelsbach, Taunus and flat-ground landing presets. The worker then runs `navigationPackage = await loadNavigationPackage()` before `ready`. If the navdata manifest or package is missing, corrupted or fails its hash check, every flight mode fails to initialize, not only the EDDF practice. The packet also does not show that a rejected `onInit` promise is caught and reported as a worker error. If it is not caught, the session waits for its load timer instead of failing explicitly. Expected: request regional navigation only where it is needed, or degrade NAV to an explicit 'database unavailable' state, and report load failure as an explicit error. Reproduction: serve a manifest with a wrong sha256, then select 'Egelsbach airborne practice'.
quality.evidence: session.ts diff: `type: 'init', kap140: true, regional_navigation: true, ...` sent unconditionally. worker.js diff: `if (msg.regional_navigation === true) navigationPackage = await loadNavigationPackage();` with no surrounding try/catch. main.ts catch comment asserts 'The worker reports a fail-closed navigation loading error', but the handler is not in the packet.

quality.description: The UI thread and the worker each fetch and verify the package independently. Nothing compares `ready.build.navigation.sha256` with the UI catalogue's sha256. If the main-thread load fails, the `.catch(() => {})` swallows it and the catalogue stays null, while the worker load can still succeed. The instruments then show 'No historical signal' while the native AP tracks real LOC/GS through NAV/APR. If the manifest changes between the two fetches, UI and AP use different data. This breaks the R-NAV-4 requirement that 'instrument and worker/AP signals use the same geometry and source data'. Expected: on ready, compare the worker's build.navigation sha/id/edition with the UI catalogue, and fail closed or disable regional guidance on a mismatch or a missing UI catalogue.
quality.evidence: main.ts diff: `void loadNavigationPackage().then(pkg => { setNavigationCatalogue(pkg); ... }).catch(() => { ... })`. worker.js loads separately and reports `build.navigation.sha256`. No comparison of the two appears anywhere in the packet.

quality.description: When altitude is not finite, the UI passes `{lat_rad: NaN, lon_rad: NaN}` and shows 'Aircraft position unavailable' for lateral VOR/LOC as well. The worker AP path calls navigationSignal with the real lat/lon, so it can still produce valid lateral guidance in that case. The instrument and the AP can therefore disagree. When no catalogue is loaded, the instrument reports 'No historical signal in modeled range' instead of an explicit 'navigation database unavailable'. Expected: identical position inputs on both paths, and an explicit reason when the database is missing.
quality.evidence: radio-nav.ts diff: `position && Number.isFinite(position.alt_msl_m) ? position : {lat_rad: NaN, lon_rad: NaN}` and `catalogue?.records ?? []`. worker.js kapSensors passes `{lat_rad, lon_rad, alt_msl_m: state[3]}`. navigation.js returns 'No historical signal in modeled range' when there are no candidates.

quality.description: The integrity pin is self-referential. The expected sha256 comes from a same-origin manifest fetched with `cache:'no-store'`, so the check detects corruption or truncation but not a coordinated substitution of package and manifest. No constant hash is pinned in code or build. The unit test compares file against manifest, not against a fixed digest. The loader also does not require the R-DATA-1 provenance fields (notice, license, source subset) to be present.

quality.description: If the regional manifest fetch or validation fails, the `.catch` only sets `regionalSettled = true`. `container.dataset.imageryRegional` becomes 'unavailable', but the user-visible status text falls back to the starter-photo branches and never says regional imagery is unavailable. R-WORLD-4 requires unavailable imagery to keep the coarse/relief layers with an explicit indication. Reproduction: make `/imagery/rhein-main/manifest.json` return 404 and place the aircraft at 50.04N 8.59E (inside OVERVIEW, outside starter DETAIL). The text is the starter outside-detail/degraded message and does not mention the regional pyramid. Expected: a visible notice that the regional detail pyramid is unavailable and coarse/starter imagery is shown.
quality.evidence: scene.ts diff: `.catch(() => { if (!disposed) { regionalSettled = true; imageryStatus(lastState); } })`. The only regional user text is `'Some regional imagery is unavailable…'` inside the `regionalLevel !== null` branch, which is unreachable when `regionalImagery` is null.

quality.description: `requestImage` ignores Cesium's `request` argument and never returns undefined for throttling. Queued tile loads can only be cancelled by whole-provider disposal or the scene signal. The FIFO `waiters` queue is unbounded, so after the camera moves, tiles that are no longer needed are still fetched, hashed and decoded ahead of newly needed tiles. Fetch concurrency is capped at six, but per-view cancellation and queue bounding are absent. That weakens the 'loading is bounded/cancellable' property and can delay detail for the current view. Expected: abort or drop queued work Cesium no longer needs, for example via the Request object or a bounded/LIFO priority queue, plus a test that moves the view mid-queue.
quality.evidence: regional-imagery.ts: `requestImage(x, y, level)` has no request parameter. `waiters.push(resolve)` has no limit. `controller.abort()` is reached only from `dispose()`. The unit test 'tile fetch concurrency is bounded and disposal aborts queued work' covers only disposal.

quality.location: app/src/regional-imagery.ts load() catch / scene.ts degraded status
quality.description: Any tile failure, including a transient `AbortSignal.timeout(12000)` expiry, is added to `failed` for the life of the provider and never retried. `failedTiles > 0` then marks the whole layer 'degraded' and shows 'Some regional imagery is unavailable' at every in-coverage position, even if the failed tile is far from the current view. Expected: bounded retry or expiry for transient failures, and a position-scoped degraded indication.
quality.evidence: `if (!disposed) { failed.add(key); ... }` with no removal path. scene.ts: `regionalStats!.failedTiles > 0 ? 'degraded'` and `if (regionalStats!.failedTiles) { outcome = 'degraded'; ... }`.

quality.description: While Stations is open in live flight, the result list is rebuilt with replaceChildren() about once per second, and distance ordering can reorder rows as the aircraft moves. The only guard against rebuilding under the user is `stationList.contains(document.activeElement)`. Safari on macOS does not focus a <button> on mouse click, and the declared target is Mac desktop browsers. A mouse or touchpad user can therefore press a 'to NAVx standby' button, have the row replaced or moved before mouseup, and lose the click or land on a different station's button. Expected: rows are stable while the pointer is over the list or a press is in progress (e.g. pause rebuilds on pointerover/pointerdown, or update distance text in place without reordering). Reproduction: Safari, live flight with nearby filter on, press a station button at about the 1 s rebuild boundary.
quality.evidence: Diff radio-nav-panel.ts: `if (!force && !reviewing && ... && (performance.now() - stationRenderedAt < 1000 || stationList.contains(document.activeElement))) return;` followed by `stationList.replaceChildren()`. The key includes `state?.lat_rad, state?.lon_rad`, so it changes on every live sample.

quality.description: The whole result list is an `aria-live="polite"` region, and its content is replaced about every second in live flight and on every changed sample in playing Review. packets.criteria_scope: Cumulative CSS of #39-#50; layout aspects of 2.0.16/2.0.18/2.0.22/2.0.42

quality.location: app/src/style.css — `.cockpit-fitted .flap-keycaps button, .cockpit-fitted .vertical-config-controls .pitch-trim-buttons button` and `.flap-keycaps button kbd, .pitch-trim-buttons button kbd`
quality.description: In the fitted cockpit, the flap and trim keycap buttons end at `font-size: 4px; height: 12px; min-height: 12px`. Their kbd glyphs are 5.5px. This later rule overrides the earlier `.cockpit-fitted` rule with the same specificity (`min-height: 24px; font-size: 11px`). The shared scale is `zoom: var(--cockpit-scale)` on a 1400px-wide `.instruments`, so at about 1440px the scale is about 1. The labels then render at about 4px, which is not readable, and the 12px-high buttons are well below a usable target size. That conflicts with 'visible labels', 'labeled nose-up/down commands' and 'controls operable'. Expected: keycap text at least about 9–10px CSS at scale 1, with targets about 24px or larger. Reproduce: at 1440×900, inspect the computed font-size and height of the flap/trim keycaps under `.cockpit-fitted`.
quality.evidence: style.css: `.cockpit-fitted .flap-keycaps button, .cockpit-fitted .vertical-config-controls .pitch-trim-buttons button { white-space: nowrap; min-height: 12px; height: 12px; padding: 0 1px; font-size: 4px; }` comes after `... { min-height: 24px; font-size: 11px; padding: 3px 1px; }`. Also `.cockpit-fitted .instruments { zoom: var(--cockpit-scale, 1); width: 1400px; }`.

quality.location: app/src/autopilot-panel.css, app/src/engine-panel.css, app/src/style.css — many cockpit labels and flags
quality.description: Many inline cockpit labels, units and flags are set at 5–6px CSS. The fitted scale is about 1 on desktop, so they render at roughly that size and are hard to read. Examples: `#ap-altitude-alert` (5px, an alert flag), `.kap-axis small` (5.5px), `.kap-dg-bug label` (5.5px), `.autopilot-heading span` (6px), engine readout labels and units (5.5px), and six-pack unit labels plus the altimeter span (5px). R-VIEW-1 requires that instruments remain readable on supported displays. Expected: a documented minimum legible size at the canonical scale, or evidence that these sizes are readable.
quality.evidence: autopilot-panel.css: `#ap-altitude-alert { ... font-size: 5px; }`, `.kap-axis small { font-size: 5.5px }`. engine-panel.css: `.engine-instrument-row .engine-readouts span { font-size: 5.5px }`. style.css: `.cockpit-fitted .six-pack .gauge-readout span { font-size: 5px; ... }`.

quality.description: Two absolutely positioned elements overlap. The altimeter-setting button is at `top: 147px; right: 5px`. The availability text is at `inset: 148px 2px auto` with an opaque background and no z-index. When availability text is shown, whichever comes later in the DOM paints on top. If that is the availability text, it covers the button, so a control is clipped or obscured. Expected: separate the two positions, or give the control an explicit stacking order. Reproduce: show the availability text in the fitted cockpit and check whether `#altimeter-open` can still be clicked.
quality.evidence: style.css: `.cockpit-fitted .pressure-altimeter #altimeter-open { position: absolute; top: 147px; right: 5px; ... }` and `.cockpit-fitted .pressure-altimeter .altimeter-availability { position: absolute; inset: 148px 2px auto; background: var(--instrument-housing); margin: 0; }`.

quality.description: The rule that moves explanatory copy to Options uses unscoped class selectors. It therefore hides these notes inside the expanded dialogs too, not only on the inline faces. Examples are `.radio-nav-dialog .radio-limitations` and `.engine-dialog .engine-flight-note`. Those dialog rules still set the notes' font sizes, which is now dead styling. R-NAV-4 requires visible historical/non-current applicability and approximate reception limits. If those are carried by `.radio-limitations` or `.nav-signal-note`, they are now hidden everywhere, including in the narrow-view collapsed panels. Expected: limit the hiding to the inline cockpit, or show evidence that the same text appears in Options.
quality.evidence: style.css: `.throttle-control p, ..., .radio-limitations, .nav-signal-note, .navigation-gauge-note, .flight-deck > footer, .engine-flight-note, .autopilot-dialog-note, .radio-dialog-note, .navigation-dialog-note, .landing-feedback > small { display: none; }`. radio-nav-panel.css: `.radio-nav-dialog ... .radio-limitations, .radio-nav-dialog .nav-signal-note { font-size: 8px; }`.

quality.description:
style.css is built by appending overrides instead of editing earlier rules. As a result:
(a) `--deck-height` is redefined about 12 times (232, 452, 450, 540, 574, 606, 520, 644, 550, 500, 530).
(b) The AP unit has conflicting fitted rules at different specificities. autopilot-panel.css (4 classes) sets heading height 11px and `#ap-status` 35px. The later style.css rules (3 classes) set 12px and 22px and lose.
(c) style.css styles `.autopilot-modes`, `.autopilot-target` and `.autopilot-inop`, but the new AP markup classes are `.kap-*`, so these rules are probably dead.
(d) `#recorded-control-details` is set to grid and later overridden with `display: block`.
(e) `#six-pack` is `display: block` and then `display: grid` in two consecutive ≤620px blocks.
(f) Several rules are duplicated, e.g. `.practice-map-panel { z-index: 6 }` twice and `.cockpit-fitted .avionics-stack` twice in one block.
(g) The unconditional `.cockpit-fitted #radio-nav-systems ...` spacing rules are overridden at ≥901px by the `body .cockpit-fitted ...` rules in radio-nav-panel.css, and radio is collapsed below 901px.
The effective layout cannot be determined without computing the cascade, which makes regressions likely. Expected: consolidate into one canonical rule set per component and remove the dead rules.

quality.location: app/tests/smoke.mjs (missing-engine runtime copy) vs app/runtime.ts RUNTIME_FILES
quality.description: The missing-engine case is meant to model a checkout where only the engine is unbuilt, but the temporary runtime root is incomplete. It copies only worker.js, altimeter.js, cockpit.js and engine.js. RUNTIME_FILES also allowlists altitude-alert.js, kap140.js, navigation.js, terrain.js and collision.js, which Codex added in #43/#46/#50. If worker.js statically imports any of these, the worker fails because those modules are missing, not because the engine is unbuilt. The test would still pass, because the jsbsim.mjs 404 assertion only checks that the request was made and every response was 404, and the notice regex only checks for /build-flight-engine/. The test comment says 'the worker's import of it fails first', but worker.js is not supplied, so this cannot be verified. This is the same weakness the earlier review raised: the case does not isolate an unbuilt engine. Expected: build the copy list from RUNTIME_FILES minus ENGINE_FILES, so the only missing files are dist/jsbsim.mjs and dist/jsbsim.wasm. Optionally also assert that no non-engine runtime request returned 404. Reproduction: remove kap140.js (or any other uncopied module) from the copy list. The test behaves identically, because it is already absent.
quality.evidence: app/tests/smoke.mjs: `for (const file of ['worker.js', 'altimeter.js', 'cockpit.js', 'engine.js']) await copyFile(...)`; app/runtime.ts: `RUNTIME_FILES = ['worker.js', 'altitude-alert.js', 'kap140.js', 'navigation.js', 'terrain.js', 'collision.js', 'altimeter.js', 'cockpit.js', 'engine.js', ...ENGINE_FILES]`

quality.description: The test comment acknowledges that a missing jsbsim.wasm with a present jsbsim.mjs is not covered. A case that removes only jsbsim.wasm would show whether instantiation failure also produces the Error state and the build instruction, rather than a hang or an unhandled rejection.

quality.description: When an allowlisted path exists but is not a regular file (for example a directory named worker.js), the middleware calls next() instead of returning 404.
